identifier_types.label: Barcode
identifier_types.description: A printed product barcode carried by a physical edition.

identifier_types.label: Matrix / runout
identifier_types.description: An inscription stamped or etched into the run-out area of a disc or the inner ring of an optical disc.

identifier_types.label: Label code
identifier_types.description: A label code assigned to an issuing label by a collecting society.

identifier_types.label: Rights society
identifier_types.description: The collecting society named on the release.

identifier_types.label: ASIN
identifier_types.description: A retailer's own product number carried on the release page.

identifier_types.label: Other
identifier_types.description: An identifier whose kind the vocabulary does not model separately; the raw type is preserved under the item's source.

identifier_types.label: Catalogue number
identifier_types.description: A catalogue number assigned by an issuing label, lifted from the release's label entries rather than from the raw identifier list.

alias_namespaces.description: Barcodes are compared as digits, so the spacing and hyphenation a submitter typed do not change the identity.
Catalogue numbers are compared without case or internal spacing, which is how labels print the same number two ways.
A matrix inscription keeps its case: the characters stamped into the disc are the evidence, so only whitespace is normalised.

normalizations.description: Keep the ASCII digits of the value in order and discard every other character.
Trim the value, collapse every run of whitespace to one space, then upper-case it.
Trim the value and collapse every run of whitespace to one space, preserving case.
